description: Kubernetes HPA and VPA in Auto mode oscillation on the same Deployment
system_prompt: You are a senior systems engineer with deep expertise in Linux internals, distributed systems, networking, and infrastructure operations. Think through the problem carefully — consider all interacting mechanisms before committing to an answer. Show your reasoning chain explicitly before stating conclusions.
user_message:
A Kubernetes Deployment (replicas: 4) has both HPA and VPA configured:

  HPA: scales on CPU utilisation, target 60%, min 2, max 10 replicas
  VPA: UpdateMode=Auto, targets the same Deployment

The system is at steady state: 4 replicas, CPU at 55%. An operator restarts
all 4 pods for an unrelated config change. After the restart:

  t=0:    4 pods restart, CPU utilisation reported at 80% (startup burst)
  t=30s:  HPA scales out to 6 replicas
  t=2m:   VPA evicts and recreates all 6 pods with higher memory/CPU requests
  t=3m:   HPA scales IN to 3 replicas (CPU utilisation % dropped after request increase)
  t=5m:   CPU utilisation rises again on 3 replicas; HPA scales out to 5
  t=7m:   VPA evicts again...
  [oscillation continues]

(a) Explain precisely why increasing VPA's resource requests causes HPA to scale in,
    tracing the specific metric and formula HPA uses.
(b) Explain why this is documented as an unsupported configuration in Kubernetes,
    not a bug to be fixed.
(c) Describe the two supported alternatives to running both simultaneously, and
    state the trade-off each makes.
